question: Can an RGB detector trained to distinguish architectural doors from furniture doors identify a room-door parent with an enclosed handle, while rejecting handled cabinets, closets, and large doorless openings?
single_change_from_pb11: Replace depth-only planar closure with a learned RGB semantic part-parent graph whose competing parent classes are door, cabinet door, and refrigerator door.

information_source.source_disjoint_boundary: The frozen detector was trained on the named DoorDetect Dataset source and is evaluated here on SUN RGB-D captures that were not used in prior PB11. The original training images are no longer present at their manifest-era path, so exact cross-source image-hash exclusion is not claimed.
information_source.license_boundary: Internal Development research only; this protocol makes no redistribution or product-license claim for the source dataset or checkpoint.

cohort_freeze.positive_admission: Official annotation contains exact door; a room-scale architectural door leaf and a handle or knob on that leaf are visibly present in RGB.
cohort_freeze.negative_admission: Official annotation contains no exact door; a handled cabinet, closet, or refrigerator-like furniture door is visibly present and is the strongest part-topology confounder.
cohort_freeze.ood_admission: Official annotation contains no exact door; a broad room or hall opening is visibly present without a door leaf spanning it.
cohort_freeze.diversity: Use at least four SUN RGB-D sensor/source buckets and at most three frames from any one bucket.
sealed_before_output: RGB, official polygon annotation, and scene metadata SHA-256
capture sequence identity and sensor/source bucket
role and human RGB audit note

inference.input: Each full source RGB image exactly once; no crops, tiles, depth, intrinsics, augmentation, test-time ensemble, or class filtering.
inference.execution_requirement: CUDA must be available and the formal result must record the actual CUDA device; otherwise stop without creating a formal result.

topology.enclosure: A handle belongs to a parent when its box center lies inside or on the parent box.
topology.assignment: Assign every enclosed handle to the smallest-area enclosing parent. Break an exact area tie by higher parent confidence, then lower class index, then lexicographically smaller x1,y1,x2,y2 coordinates.
topology.authorization: DOOR_HANDLE_TOPOLOGY is true if and only if at least one detected handle is assigned to a detected class-0 door parent.
topology.negative_competition: A handle assigned to cabinet door or refrigerator door does not authorize. A door box with no assigned handle does not authorize.

metrics: per-frame detections and deterministic parent assignments

gate.development_promotion: All 4/4 architectural-door positives authorize, all 0/2 handled-furniture negatives authorize, all 0/2 large-opening OOD controls authorize, and balanced accuracy is 1.0.
gate.pass: Record a Development gate met, freeze checkpoint plus topology unchanged, and run one new source-disjoint confirmation cohort.
gate.fail: Close this checkpoint/topology pair on the frozen cohort and change the information source or representation; do not tune it on these pixels.

forbidden_rescue: After any cohort model output, do not change rows, roles, checkpoint, image size, confidence, NMS IoU, maximum detections, crop or tile policy, parent classes, center-in-parent rule, assignment tie-breaks, authorization rule, or gate; do not run alternate epochs, checkpoints, YOLO sizes, thresholds, crops, prompt models, or fusion on these pixels.
claim_boundary: PB12 is a current-frame RGB architectural-door part-topology Development experiment. Even a pass is not exact target ownership, public access, open or closed actuation state, metric traversability, active-view causality, temporal persistence, guidance, arrival, product benefit, user benefit, or safety evidence.
